decision.what_is_decided: Whether a Playwright console message is kept as a run diagnostic, based only on its already-labeled type.

inputs.name: console_message_type
inputs.role: Closed type tag used as a keep-or-drop filter

decision.downstream_action: recordEvent appends a truncated text snippet to consoleEvents returned with the run.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: The keep test is equality on Playwright’s console type tag; message wording is never interpreted.

context_dependence.evidence: Filter does not use the user task, page excerpt, history, or action space.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: A two-value membership test on an engine-supplied enum fully specifies the filter.

judgment_required.evidence: Severity is already classified by the browser/Playwright before this callback runs.

rule_stability.evidence: Console type names are a stable Playwright contract, not a site- or task-specific policy.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: This only caps diagnostic logging; it does not gate navigation or safety.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: msg.text is sliced for storage only; it is not an input to the keep/drop test.

decision_complexity.evidence: Single early-return on type; no competing outcomes or tradeoffs.

observed.claim: The callback drops console events unless Playwright already tagged them as error or warning.

evidence.observation: On console, type is read and any type other than those two names returns without recording.

observed.claim: Message body is truncated and stored after the type filter; it does not affect the filter.

evidence.observation: When kept, text is sliced to a fixed length and passed to recordEvent with the page URL slice.

inferred.claim: This is diagnostic plumbing, not a judgment about the task, matching the file’s code-vs-Jev split.

evidence.observation: File comment states code owns control flow and Jev owns judgments.
Observers only collect console, pageerror, and requestfailed diagnostics for the run result.

unknown: Whether the developer considered asking Jev which console lines matter for the task.
Whether noisy-but-typed warnings were ever a problem they wanted to filter semantically.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: The Jev site interprets task plus live page to pick an action and grade done/stuck; this callback never sees that state.

evidence.observation: askJev is given task, page excerpt, elements, and history, then stepQuestions.
The console handler only reads Playwright message type and truncated text.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Outcomes here are keep-or-drop of a log line, not competing browser actions or graded noul.

evidence.observation: Jev answers supply action choice plus goal_done and stuck noul used as stop gates.
Kept events are pushed onto a capped consoleEvents array.

decision.what_is_decided: Which Vercel AI SDK client (or none) will generate text to type, based on env config and API-key shape.

inputs.name: type_provider_env
inputs.role: Optional explicit provider name that reorders the candidate list

inputs.name: type_model_env
inputs.role: Optional model id passed into the chosen SDK factory

inputs.name: compatible_base_url
inputs.role: If set, short-circuits to an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint

inputs.name: provider_api_keys
inputs.source: process.env keys for openai, openrouter, anthropic, google/gemini (src/navigate.ts:158-165)
inputs.role: Presence, length, and prefix regex select which candidate wins

decision.downstream_action: generateTextToType uses the client to propose fill text, or falls back to heuristicQuery when null or on error.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Provider ids and key-prefix regexes are conventional identifiers, not open-ended task language.

context_dependence.evidence: Depends on process env for this run, not on the page, DOM, or natural-language task.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Fixed candidate table, optional reorder, length check, and prefix test uniquely pick one client or null.

judgment_required.evidence: No ranking of which model is best for the task; first matching configured key wins.

rule_stability.evidence: Rules are exact today but rest on vendor key-prefix conventions that could change outside this repo.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Selects a typing backend from caller-supplied secrets; no safety or content policy.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Function never reads the task string or page text; only env strings and key shapes.

decision_complexity.evidence: One short-circuit then a linear scan of four hardcoded providers.

observed.claim: A custom base-URL env, if present, always wins and builds a compatible client with a default model id.

evidence.observation: baseUrl from env causes an immediate return of a named compatible-endpoint model.

observed.claim: Otherwise a fixed provider list is scanned; a key longer than 20 that matches that provider’s prefix regex returns that client.

evidence.observation: Candidates for openai, openrouter, anthropic, and google each have a test regex, factory, and default model; first key match returns.

observed.claim: No match yields null, and the caller then uses a keyword heuristic instead of any model.

evidence.observation: Function returns null after the loop.
generateTextToType treats a missing generator as heuristicQuery with via keyword-heuristic.

inferred.claim: This is SDK wiring from secrets, not a semantic pick of what to type or which browser action to take.

evidence.observation: Comment frames the block as a provider-agnostic typing generator via the Vercel AI SDK.
Task and element description are only used later inside generateText, not inside resolveGeneratorModel.

unknown: Why typing uses a separate AI SDK path instead of a Jev question for the string to type.
Whether the developer considered Jev for provider selection; absence of Jev here does not show it would be wrong.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Jev chooses among page actions from task and DOM; this function never inspects the page or task.

evidence.observation: askJev state includes task, current_page, excerpt, interactive_elements, and history.
resolveGeneratorModel reads only env vars and key strings.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Outcomes are SDK clients identified by closed provider names, not competing action ids or noul grades.

evidence.observation: Return value is a model instance plus a provider label string.
Jev outcomes drive proposed action and numeric stop gates for done and stuck.

decision.what_is_decided: Which extractor to run for the final page payload, given a caller-supplied format name.

inputs.name: format
inputs.role: Enum selecting html, aria, markdown, or plain-text extraction

inputs.name: maxChars
inputs.source: options.maxChars or DEFAULT_CAPS for that format (src/navigate.ts:69-74, 310)
inputs.role: Hard cap used only to slice and flag truncation, not to choose a format

inputs.name: page
inputs.source: Playwright Page after the navigation loop (src/navigate.ts:549-553)
inputs.role: DOM/source being serialized; not classified, only read

outcomes: markdown via turndown of body html
decision.downstream_action: Returned as the run’s page payload (truncated) to CLI/MCP callers.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Format is a four-value option type; each name maps to one extractor with no interpretation.

context_dependence.evidence: Branching does not depend on task success, page meaning, or history—only the format argument.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Equality on three named formats plus an else branch fully specifies the mapping.

judgment_required.evidence: The caller already chose the representation; this function only implements it.

rule_stability.evidence: The format union is part of the public options type; adding a format would be an API change.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Serialization of the final DOM; no access, safety, or goal judgment.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Page text/html is copied or converted, not read to decide what the page means.

decision_complexity.evidence: Straight if/else chain with one extractor per format and a shared truncate.

observed.claim: Format string equality selects one of four extractors; anything else uses body innerText.

evidence.observation: html, aria, and markdown each have a dedicated branch; the else branch evaluates innerText.

observed.claim: After extraction, content is only measured and sliced to maxChars.

evidence.observation: Return records truncated flag, true length, and a sliced content string.

observed.claim: format is an input option with a default, not something computed from the page.

evidence.observation: NavigateOptions types format as a four-literal union.
navigate defaults format to text and looks up a default cap from DEFAULT_CAPS.

inferred.claim: This is output formatting after the Jev loop, not a substitute for judging whether the goal holds.

evidence.observation: extractPayload runs once after the step loop, using the already-chosen format.
File comment assigns judgments to Jev and control flow to code.

unknown: Whether anyone considered letting Jev pick the most useful page representation.
Caller motives for choosing a given format at the CLI/MCP boundary (importers not required for this contrast).

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Jev is used mid-loop to choose the next action and stop; extractPayload runs after the loop to serialize whatever page remains.

evidence.observation: askJev with stepQuestions is inside the step loop before acting.
extractPayload is called once on the final page after the loop ends.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: There is no open-ended match of task language to controls; each format name has exactly one extractor.

evidence.observation: Three equality tests plus else fully determine the extraction method.
Jev state includes free-form task and a list of competing interactive elements.
